sections.title: Geography of Opportunity
sections.description: This course is designed to explore the subfield of urban geography and its use in education and higher education scholarship. Readings will cover theoretical and conceptual foundations such as postcolonial theory, nationalism, Black geographies, and AfroLatin American hemispheric thought. Students will engage in ethnographic research methods for their culminating paper, exploring the City of Philadelphia and its “education” landscape. We engage questions such as: What does educational opportunity consist of in Philadelphia? How do we define the construct of education? How is opportunity conceived? What are the spatial and non-spatial parameters?

sections.title: Geography of Opportunity: Exploring College Access and University-Assisted Community School Partners
sections.description: Geography of Opportunity is an ABCS course that brings together urban geography, ethnographic research methods, and college access scholarship to examine how opportunity is spatially produced and experienced in Philadelphia. The course is grounded in previous teaching and research that began in Ferguson, Missouri, anchored in theoretical traditions of resistance and change - including Black Geographies, postcolonial theory, cultural-ecology, and Third Space - and asks students to apply these or alternative frameworks through original field-based research. In this course, students design and conduct their own qualitative studies using ethnographic field observations, and photographic documentation. A key collaboration for this course is its ongoing partnership with University-Assisted Community Schools (UACS) through the Netter Center for Community Partnerships. Students will become familiar with UACS and choose a site for their fieldwork, or another site of choice within Philadelphia. Past student field sites have included beauty salons, bookstores, parks and community centers.
